repo_notes.content: moqtail/moqtail is a Draft 22 MOQ Transport (MOQT) monorepo combining a Rust workspace (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock at root) and an npm workspace (package.json, package-lock.json at root). Top-level folders: 'libs' (protocol libraries: moqtail-rs, moqtail-ts, moqtail-ssts), 'apps' (relay server and client applications: relay, client, client-js, meet), 'dev/conformance' (machine-readable conformance data for the current draft: draft22), 'scripts' (release/commit tooling, client test script, and conformance/performance test scripts), plus .changeset (release automation), .github (CI/CD workflows), .husky (git hooks), and cert generation under apps/relay/cert. The relay server is published as a Docker image to ghcr.io/moqtail/relay. License is Apache-2.0. Citation/academic reference: Gurel, Ugur, Begen, 'MOQtail: open-source, IETF-compliant MOQT protocol libraries,' ACM MMSys 2026.

Two parallel implementations of the same protocol exist side by side: moqtail-rs (Rust, libs/moqtail-rs, used by the relay and native client) and moqtail-ts (TypeScript, libs/moqtail-ts, npm package 'moqtail', used by the browser client and meet demo app). main tracks Draft 22 of the IETF MOQ Transport spec (older drafts live on the draft-14, draft-16, and draft-18 branches); conformance data is under dev/conformance/draft22/. When documenting protocol concepts, prefer linking both implementations rather than treating one as canonical.

libs/moqtail-ts has two halves: the MOQT client (MOQtailClient, entries 'moqtail', 'moqtail/client', 'moqtail/model', 'moqtail/util') and an MSF/CMSF player for the browser (entries 'moqtail/player' and 'moqtail/player/component', the <moqtail-video> web component). apps/client-js (player.moqtail.dev) plays through <moqtail-video> inside a Video.js v10 skin.

Versioning uses changesets (.changeset directory); the Rust packages moqtail-rs, relay, client, and moqtail-ssts are linked. Libraries are published to npm and crates.io. The relay server is published as a container image to ghcr.io/moqtail/relay via the relay.yml workflow. CI is GitHub Actions with separate workflows for Rust (rust.yml), JS (js.yml), misc checks (misc.yml), player checks (player.yml), meet checks (meet.yml), relay checks and container image building (relay.yml), and releases to crates.io/npm (release-rust.yml, release.yml).

pages.title: MOQtail Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the MOQtail project: what Media-over-QUIC (MOQ) is, why MOQtail exists, the components it ships (moqtail-rs, moqtail-ts, relay, client apps), and how they fit together as a Draft 22 MOQT toolkit.

page_notes.content: Source primarily from the root README.md, which summarizes the TypeScript and Rust libraries, the Relay (WebTransport and raw QUIC on the same port), Getting Started prerequisites/installation, branch status for older drafts, and the academic citation block. Mention the live demo at player.moqtail.dev and the project topics (streaming, real-time, media, MOQ).

pages.title: Repository Structure
pages.purpose: Explain the monorepo organization: the Cargo workspace vs the npm workspace, the top-level libs/ and apps/ directories, the dev/ and scripts/ support directories, and how Rust and TypeScript components relate to and depend on each other.

page_notes.content: Document the dual workspace setup: root Cargo.toml defines the Rust workspace members: apps/relay, apps/client, libs/moqtail-rs, libs/moqtail-ssts; shared dependency versions (including the internal moqtail and moqtail-ssts path deps) are centralized under [workspace.dependencies] and member crates reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Root package.json defines npm workspaces via wildcard patterns: apps/*, libs/* (resolving to libs/moqtail-ts, apps/client-js, apps/meet). dev/conformance/draft22/ holds JSON conformance data (message, parameter, property, error/termination codes, varint vectors). Note .vscode, .editorconfig, .prettierrc (root plus per-package copies), rustfmt.toml, commitlint.config.ts, lint-staged.config.js as shared tooling config that spans both languages. Root package.json orchestrates npm scripts across workspaces.

pages.title: MOQ Protocol Basics
pages.purpose: Overview of the Media-over-QUIC (MOQT) protocol as defined by IETF draft-ietf-moq-transport (Draft 22 on main), and the core data model concepts: tracks, namespaces, groups, objects, subscriptions, and fetch.

page_notes.content: Frame this as protocol/domain documentation rather than implementation documentation — it should explain MOQT concepts (control vs data streams, tracks/groups/objects, publisher/subscriber/relay roles, LOC and CMSF media formats mentioned in the repo description) independent of language, then point readers to the Rust and TypeScript library pages for implementation specifics. Cite the IETF draft-ietf-moq-transport spec for protocol terminology.

pages.title: Protocol Libraries
pages.purpose: Section landing page documenting the core protocol implementation libraries shared across the codebase, in both Rust and TypeScript.

page_notes.content: Acts as a parent/index page linking to moqtail-rs, Control Stream Handler, Data Stream Handler, moqtail-ts, Client API, Player, Web Component, Elements and Extensions, Buffer and ABR Controllers, and Playout Buffer child pages. Also mention libs/moqtail-ssts (switching-set support used by the relay's apps/relay/src/server/ssts module).

pages.title: moqtail-rs (Rust Library)
pages.purpose: Detailed documentation of the Rust protocol library at libs/moqtail-rs/: crate architecture, module layout, key dependencies (e.g. wtransport/quinn for WebTransport and raw QUIC, serialization), and the public API surface consumed by the relay and native client.

page_notes.content: Start from libs/moqtail-rs/README.md. The crate exposes client, model, relay, and transport modules (plus a conformance module checked against dev/conformance data). The model module contains catalog, common, control, data, error, parameter, and property sub-modules. The transport module contains connection.rs (WebTransport and raw QUIC connection abstraction), control_stream_handler.rs, and data_stream_handler.rs. Cross-link to the Control Stream Handler and Data Stream Handler pages.

pages.title: Control Stream Handler
pages.purpose: Documentation of control message exchange in moqtail-rs: serialization/deserialization of MOQT control messages (SETUP, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, etc.), timeout handling, and the control-plane communication layer used by both relay and client.

page_notes.content: Located at libs/moqtail-rs/src/transport/control_stream_handler.rs. Document the message enum/struct types, the read/write loop, and how timeouts and malformed-message errors are surfaced to callers (relay Session Management and Message Handlers pages depend on this).

pages.title: Data Stream Handler
pages.purpose: Documentation of data stream transmission and reception in moqtail-rs, including the stream abstractions used for object delivery over QUIC/WebTransport streams.

page_notes.content: Located at libs/moqtail-rs/src/transport/data_stream_handler.rs. Document the send/receive data stream APIs, group/object framing on the wire, and how these are consumed by the relay's Track and Subscription system as well as client publisher/subscriber/fetcher modes.

pages.title: moqtail-ts (TypeScript Library)
pages.purpose: Detailed documentation of the TypeScript library: the MOQT client and the MSF/CMSF player, package structure and entries, build system (tsdown, api-extractor), browser/WebTransport integration, and how it's consumed by client-js and the meet app.

page_notes.content: Start from libs/moqtail-ts/README.md (npm package name 'moqtail'). Entries, from libs/moqtail-ts/package.json exports: 'moqtail' (client, model and util, no player), 'moqtail/client', 'moqtail/model', 'moqtail/util', 'moqtail/player' (src/player/index.ts) and 'moqtail/player/component' (src/player/component/index.ts). Built with tsdown (tsdown.config.ts) and checked with api-extractor. Valibot is the only runtime dependency; custom-media-element and media-tracks are optional peer dependencies used by the web component. Browsers: Chrome and Safari 26.4+ (WebTransport). Targets MOQT draft-22 and the MSF and CMSF editor's drafts. Verify usage examples against the current README and source.

pages.title: Client API
pages.purpose: Documentation of the public client API in moqtail-ts: connection setup, subscribe/fetch operations, publication and namespace management, and request/response handling.

page_notes.content: Verify public API examples and exact method signatures against libs/moqtail-ts/src/client and libs/moqtail-ts/README.md. Cover `new MOQtailClient(options)` (no I/O) and `await client.init()` (connects); events through `client.on(event, listener)` / `client.off()`, with any number of listeners (ClientEvents in src/client/types.ts, e.g. messagesent, messagereceived, dataevent, sessionterminated, orderinggap); `client.subscribe` returning `{ requestId, subscribeOk, stream, done }`, where `done` resolves with the PUBLISH_DONE that ended it; `client.fetch` returning `{ requestId, fetchOk, stream }`; and the per-request object ordering option (`ordering` on the client, subscribe and fetch options, src/client/ordering.ts). Document error handling through RequestError.

pages.title: Player
pages.purpose: Documentation of MOQtailPlayer, the MSF/CMSF player in moqtail-ts: building a chain from a moqt:// URL, its state and events, errors, and the built-in catalog, timeline, CMAF source and MSE sink elements.

page_notes.content: MOQtailPlayer is libs/moqtail-ts/src/player/player.ts. The chain is built with `.source(uri)`, an optional `.transform(element)`, and `.sink(video)` (the MSE sink), then `init()`, `play()`, `pause()`, `seek()`, `destroy()`. State machine in src/player/state.ts, events in PlayerEvents (statechange, error, warning, catalog, renditionchange, streamtypechange, reconnecting, ...). PlayerError and its codes and categories are in src/player/error.ts. MSF URLs (`moqt://...#msf:<namespace>--<track>`) are parsed by src/player/msf_url.ts. Players on the same origin share one client (src/player/client_slot.ts). Built-in elements: catalog parsing with Valibot (src/player/elements/catalog/), the media timeline (src/player/elements/mediatimeline/) and SAP timeline (src/player/elements/saptimeline/), the CMAF source (src/player/elements/cmaf/) and the MSE sink (src/player/elements/mse/).

pages.title: Web Component
pages.purpose: Documentation of <moqtail-video>, the video-backed custom element that plays a moqt:// URL and implements HTMLMediaElement and the media-ui-extensions IDL.

page_notes.content: Code: libs/moqtail-ts/src/player/component/ (element.ts, renditions.ts; `defineMOQtailVideo()` in index.ts). Built on custom-media-element and media-tracks. Document the attributes (`src`, `switch-from`, plus the usual video attributes such as autoplay and preload), the `config` property (MOQtailPlayerOptions, read on each load), the `player` property, the media-ui-extensions additions (streamType, liveEdgeStart, targetLiveWindow, video renditions), and that it installs the default plugins: `liveBuffer()` is the only plugin when `config.plugins` is empty or unset; a non-empty list is taken as written, so leaving `liveBuffer()` out disables it. apps/client-js/src/lib/videojs.ts shows the Video.js v10 integration.

pages.title: Elements and Extensions
pages.purpose: Documentation of the player's element model: element definitions, pads and packets, negotiation and probing, element interfaces, and extensions that bundle elements with setup options.

page_notes.content: Code: libs/moqtail-ts/src/player/element/ (define.ts for `defineElement`, base.ts for SourceElement / TransformElement / SinkElement, pad.ts for pads, items, events and signals, negotiation.ts for probing and capability matching, chain.ts, context.ts, interfaces.ts for MEDIA_SOURCE and MEDIA_SINK). Probes return a boolean; among those that accept, the lower `priority` wins, then registered elements, plugins' in plugin order, then built-ins. Custom elements are added with `player.registerElement(definition)`. Plugins are created with `definePlugin` (src/player/plugin.ts) and passed in `opts.plugins`: each has `init(config)`, `setup` (adds setup parameters), `negotiated` (checks SERVER_SETUP; a rejected plugin contributes nothing), `priority`, and `features(ctx)`: elements, switch sources and a buffer controller. `ssts()` (src/player/plugins/ssts/) offers sender-side track switching at setup; the catalog probes the active switch sources with each media set's first track and loads the first that accepts (SstsSource) with the probed element as its child.

pages.title: Buffer and ABR Controllers
pages.purpose: Documentation of the pluggable controllers that steer playback: the BufferController interface and the default latency/buffer controller, and the planned ABR controller.

page_notes.content: Code: libs/moqtail-ts/src/player/plugins/buffer/ (index.ts for the `liveBuffer()` plugin, live.ts for its controller) and src/player/plugin.ts for the BufferController interface. A buffer controller is a plugin feature: the first active plugin (by priority, then list order) offering one is attached to the media sink while a ready stream is live. `liveBuffer` has priority Infinity, so any other buffer plugin wins. MOQtailPlayer installs none by default, while <moqtail-video> installs `liveBuffer()`. An ABR controller isn't implemented yet: rendition switching is manual (or done by the relay under SSTS).

pages.title: Playout Buffer
pages.purpose: Documentation of the Meet app's playout buffer, which smooths out network jitter for WebCodecs playback.

page_notes.content: The playout buffer lives at apps/meet/src/lib/playout_buffer.ts and is used by the Meet App only. Document its latency targets, how it reads from the Client API's subscribe stream, and how it hands frames to WebCodecs decoding. The MSF player doesn't use it; for the player's latency and buffer control see Buffer and ABR Controllers.

pages.title: Relay Server
pages.purpose: Comprehensive documentation of the relay server architecture — the most critical component, responsible for forwarding MOQT control and data messages between publishers and subscribers. Includes how to run it locally and as a container.

page_notes.content: The relay lives under apps/relay/ (entry point apps/relay/src/main.rs, implementation under apps/relay/src/server/). It accepts WebTransport and raw QUIC on the same UDP port, demultiplexed by ALPN. Root README gives the run commands: `cargo run -p relay -- --port 4433 --cert-file apps/relay/cert/cert.pem --key-file apps/relay/cert/key.pem` locally, and a `docker run` of ghcr.io/moqtail/relay:latest mounting the cert/key into /certs. Local image build: `docker build -f apps/relay/Dockerfile -t moqtail-relay .` from the workspace root. Images are published by .github/workflows/relay.yml with `latest` and version tags from `relay@*` releases, plus branch and commit SHA tags for CI builds. Certificate generation/browser trust setup is documented in apps/relay/cert/README.md — link to it rather than duplicating.

pages.title: Server Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the relay server's internal architecture: the Server/Session model, how incoming WebTransport/QUIC connections are accepted, and the concurrent (async) processing pattern used per session.

page_notes.content: The entry point is apps/relay/src/main.rs; the server is apps/relay/src/server.rs (modules under apps/relay/src/server/) with config in apps/relay/src/server/config.rs. Document how it binds the QUIC/WebTransport listener using cert-file/key-file CLI args, and how it spawns per-session work (apps/relay/src/server/session.rs). Cross-link to Session Management for per-connection detail and to Client Management for the registry that spans sessions.

pages.title: Session Management
pages.purpose: Documentation of session lifecycle: connection establishment/teardown, SessionContext state, and control-stream message processing loop for a single client connection.

page_notes.content: Code: apps/relay/src/server/session.rs and session_context.rs (plus request_stream.rs). Document SessionContext fields (client identity, negotiated parameters, associated streams), the control-stream read loop (built on moqtail-rs's Control Stream Handler), and graceful/error teardown paths. Note interactions with ClientManager for registering/deregistering sessions.

pages.title: Client Management
pages.purpose: Documentation of the MOQTClient abstraction in the relay, partitioned stream management for scaling outbound delivery, message queuing, and the ClientManager registry that tracks all connected clients.

page_notes.content: Code: apps/relay/src/server/client.rs and client_manager.rs. Document how MOQTClient wraps a session's outbound data streams (partitioned for parallelism), the queuing/backpressure strategy, and how ClientManager is looked up by Track/Subscription processing when fanning out objects to subscribers.

pages.title: Track and Subscription System
pages.purpose: Section landing page explaining how tracks manage content distribution from publishers and how subscriptions handle per-client delivery, caching, and filtering.

page_notes.content: Index/parent page linking Track Management, Subscription Processing, Caching System, and Message Handlers — together these form the relay's data-plane logic.

pages.title: Track Management
pages.purpose: Documentation of the Track abstraction: subscriber registration/removal, event distribution via partitioned channels, and object logging for replay/caching.

page_notes.content: Code: apps/relay/src/server/track.rs, track_manager.rs, and object_logger.rs. Document the Track struct's subscriber list, the partitioned broadcast-channel mechanism used to fan out newly published objects without a single bottleneck, and how published objects are logged/handed to the Caching System for fetch support.

pages.title: Subscription Processing
pages.purpose: Documentation of subscription lifecycle (Subscribe -> active -> Unsubscribe/error), filtering of objects by group/object location ranges, per-subscription stream management, and the subscription state machine.

page_notes.content: Code: apps/relay/src/server/subscription.rs, subscription_manager.rs, prefix_subscription.rs, filter_constructor.rs, and seen_objects.rs. Document the state machine driving a subscription (pending/active/ended), how SUBSCRIBE filter parameters (e.g. start/end group-object location) are applied to incoming objects, and how a subscription's data stream is opened/closed against the Data Stream Handler from moqtail-rs.

pages.title: Caching System
pages.purpose: Documentation of the TrackCache, built on the moka caching library: eviction policies (TTL/TTI), object storage organized by group, and how the cache backs Fetch (on-demand) requests.

page_notes.content: Code: apps/relay/src/server/track_cache.rs (plus fetch_request.rs and fill.rs). Document TrackCache's use of moka for TTL/TTI-based eviction, the per-group object storage layout, and how a FETCH control message is resolved against cached objects versus live data. Cross-link to Configuration and Deployment for cache size/TTL configuration knobs.

pages.title: Message Handlers
pages.purpose: Documentation of control message processing in the relay: SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, PUBLISH, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, and TRACK_STATUS handlers, and the relay (forwarding) logic that ties publishers to subscribers.

page_notes.content: Handlers live in apps/relay/src/server/message_handlers/ (subscribe_handler.rs, fetch_handler.rs, publish_handler.rs, publish_namespace_handler.rs, subscribe_namespace_handler.rs, subscribe_tracks_handler.rs, track_status_handler.rs, with shared parameter handling in parameters.rs and dispatch in mod.rs). Document each handler's responsibilities and teardown paths, and how handlers depend on ClientManager, Track Management, Subscription Processing, and the Caching System.

pages.title: Configuration and Deployment
pages.purpose: Documentation of relay server configuration: command-line options (port, cert-file, key-file), cache settings, network parameters, TLS certificate setup, and container deployment.

page_notes.content: Document CLI flags shown in the README (`--port`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`) plus any additional options defined in apps/relay/src/server/config.rs (e.g. cache TTL/size, log level). Document the GHCR image tagging scheme from .github/workflows/relay.yml: `latest` and version tags from `relay@*` releases, plus branch and commit SHA tags for CI builds. Link to apps/relay/cert/README.md for local cert generation / browser trust.

pages.title: Client Applications
pages.purpose: Section landing page for the client applications that act as publishers or subscribers against the relay: the browser client, the native Rust client, and the Meet video-conferencing demo.

page_notes.content: Index/parent page linking Browser Client (client-js), Native Client (client), and Meet App.

pages.title: Browser Client (client-js)
pages.purpose: Documentation of the Preact-based browser client (player.moqtail.dev): playback through <moqtail-video> in a Video.js v10 skin, the opt-in Advanced panel, and the CMAF publisher.

page_notes.content: Located at apps/client-js/. Playback goes through the library's <moqtail-video> inside a Video.js v10 skin (src/lib/videojs.ts, src/components/VideoPlayer.tsx); there's an opt-in Advanced panel (src/components/Advanced.tsx). Document the UI component tree (Header, Sidebar, VideoPlayer, PublisherPanel, Advanced). WebCodecs is used only on the publisher side, to encode before CMAF muxing (src/lib/cmaf-muxer.ts); the publisher (src/lib/publisher.ts) writes an MSF catalog.

pages.title: Native Client (client)
pages.purpose: Documentation of the Rust-based native client supporting publisher, subscriber, and fetcher modes via a command-line interface, built on moqtail-rs and supporting both WebTransport (https://) and raw QUIC (moqt://) server URLs.

page_notes.content: Located at apps/client/. Document the CLI argument surface (e.g. `cargo run --bin client -- -c publish --server https://127.0.0.1:4433` or `moqt://...`) and how each mode maps to moqtail-rs's Control Stream Handler and Data Stream Handler. For raw QUIC, authority/path are sent as CLIENT_SETUP parameters.

pages.title: Meet App (Video Conferencing Demo)
pages.purpose: Documentation of the React-based video conferencing demo: the media pipeline, WebCodecs-based encoding/decoding, signalling carried over MOQ tracks, and Playout Buffer integration for synchronized playback.

page_notes.content: Located at apps/meet/. Document how signalling (room membership, track announcements) is carried over MOQ tracks, how WebCodecs is used for encoding and decoding, and how it differs from apps/client-js.

pages.title: Development Guide
pages.purpose: Comprehensive guide for developers contributing to MOQtail: environment setup, prerequisites, and day-to-day workflows across the Rust and TypeScript workspaces.

page_notes.content: Base prerequisites per README: Rust toolchain, Node.js 22+, npm, and Docker (for relay container builds/runs). Setup: `git clone https://github.com/moqtail/moqtail.git && cd moqtail && npm install`. Commit requirements (enforced by Husky hooks and CI): every commit must include a `Signed-off-by` line (DCO — Developer Certificate of Origin, appended via `git commit -s`); commit messages must follow Conventional Commits format; user-facing changes require a changeset (prompted by pre-commit hook). A CLA may be requested for significant contributions. Full details in CONTRIBUTING.md.

pages.title: Build System
pages.purpose: Documentation of the build process: the Cargo workspace (Rust crates), npm workspaces (TypeScript packages/apps), and how cross-language dependencies (e.g. shared protocol constants or generated types) are kept consistent.

page_notes.content: Cargo workspace (from root Cargo.toml) members: apps/relay, apps/client, libs/moqtail-rs, libs/moqtail-ssts; dependency versions are pinned once in [workspace.dependencies] and inherited by members with `dep.workspace = true`. npm workspace (from root package.json) uses wildcard patterns: apps/* and libs/* (resolving to libs/moqtail-ts, apps/client-js, apps/meet). Root package.json scripts orchestrate builds (`npm run build` builds libs/moqtail-ts, then apps/client-js and apps/meet), tests (`npm test` runs vitest for libs/moqtail-ts), and formatting. All helper scripts live under scripts/: release/commit tooling (postversion.mjs, precommit.mjs), test-client.sh, and conformance/performance scripts (conformance-test.sh, perf-test.sh with perf-test.env.example). Conformance data is under dev/conformance/draft22/.

pages.title: Testing Strategy
pages.purpose: Documentation of the testing infrastructure: vitest for TypeScript packages, Rust unit/integration tests via cargo test, and any cross-language or end-to-end integration testing approach.

page_notes.content: Document npm test scripts and Vitest configuration in libs/moqtail-ts/, `cargo test` usage per crate, the moqtail-rs conformance module checked against dev/conformance data, and scripts/conformance-test.sh / scripts/perf-test.sh. Cross-reference .github/workflows/rust.yml and js.yml (badged in the README as 'Rust Checks' and 'JavaScript Checks') for how tests run in CI, including any relay-vs-client interop testing (scripts/test-client.sh). moqtail-ts also has real-browser tests (libs/moqtail-ts/vitest.browser.config.ts, test/browser/), run with `npm run test:browser` in headless Chrome through Playwright against the test sources on relay.moqtail.dev; Safari is tested manually before release.

pages.title: CI/CD Pipeline
pages.purpose: Documentation of GitHub Actions workflows: pull request checks (Rust and JavaScript), release automation (changesets-driven publishing), container image builds/pushes to GHCR, and documentation deployment.

page_notes.content: Eight workflows exist under .github/workflows/: rust.yml (Rust format/lint/test), js.yml (JavaScript checks), misc.yml (miscellaneous checks), player.yml (client-js checks), meet.yml (meet app checks), relay.yml (relay checks and GHCR image build/push), release-rust.yml (crates.io releases), and release.yml (npm releases via changesets). Verify details against the workflow files; relay images go to ghcr.io/moqtail/relay.

pages.title: Versioning and Releases
pages.purpose: Documentation of the changesets-based release workflow: semantic versioning, linked/grouped packages, and publishing to npm (TypeScript) and crates.io (Rust), plus relay container image releases.

page_notes.content: Document the changeset authoring flow (adding a changeset per PR), how linked packages are configured in .changeset/config.json (moqtail-rs, relay, client, and moqtail-ssts are linked and bumped together), and the release tag convention `relay@x.y.z` used to trigger relay image publishing.

pages.title: Code Quality Tools
pages.purpose: Documentation of linting, formatting, commit message conventions, and pre-commit hooks enforced across the project.

page_notes.content: Document Prettier (root .prettierrc plus per-package copies in libs/moqtail-ts, apps/client-js, apps/meet) and rustfmt (rustfmt.toml) as the formatters for TS and Rust respectively, .editorconfig for cross-editor consistency, commitlint.config.ts for enforced Conventional Commits format, lint-staged.config.js for staged-file checks, and .husky/ git hooks that wire these into contributor workflows.
